His going away to the Father, and (to use a term which often
occurs elsewhere in St. John's gospel) His glorification. In
setting Him aside by crucifying Him, the world confirms His
own word that He does not belong to it, and without its
own knowledge and desire it must thus glorify Him. All this
of course is only visible to one whose eyes the Spirit has
opened, and who in consequence sees righteousness and
victory where the world sees defeat and condemnation.
Christianity too has often fallen a prey to the temptation to
detect its triumphs in the sphere of the visible and to insist
on this tangible evidence. Thus people speak of the influence
of Christ on the course of world history, of the effects which
His spirit has had on human manners and morals, of its
uplifting and civilizing influence on nations. The world war
showed little of all this, and, since it was a war between
nominally Christian peoples, many so-called Christians and
many pagans became bewildered about Christianity. Rightly
so! For we are disastrously wrong when we wish to see the
victory and righteousness of Christ manifested in the visible
sphere. The world which does not apprehend His true
victory answers of course: "Imagination! Fancy!" It does not
know that what it declares to be imagination and fancy can
be the strongest, most abiding of all realities, and that the
things which it deems great and secure are but dreams which
the breath of eternity disperses.
And finally the Spirit will convince the world of "judg-
ment". The world too speaks about judgment, and means
thereby the judgment which world history pronounces, and
which is embodied within the earthly sphere. But Scripture
means something quite different: "of judgment, because the
ruler of this world is judged." The world which fondly
imagines that it is a closed circle, complete in itself, which
supposes that it is responsible only to itself, and which
subjects to its unconditioned claim all that belongs to it-
this world as a whole is summoned before the judgment of
God and is there judged, because it rejects the One who
over against it voices the claim of the Eternal.
